name: Do older Denver homes require special considerations for fixture replacement?

mainEntity.name: Do older Denver homes require special considerations for fixture replacement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, older Denver area homes—especially those built before the 1980s in neighborhoods like Denver, Englewood, or Littleton—often contain galvanized steel pipes, aging copper, or cast iron drains. These legacy materials can corrode internally or strip threads when disconnected. Connecting modern brass or PEX fixtures to older piping frequently requires transitional fittings or replacing corroded shutoff valves. During initial assessments, contractors inspect exposed supply stops beneath sinks and access panels to identify deteriorated lines before disassembly begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. Older Denver homes may feature galvanized steel or brittle copper lines that need transitional fittings, new shutoff valves, or localized pipe upgrades.
